methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $2M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Ground Control Development, led by founder Lizzy Manzi, is a seed-stage company in the Housing & Construction sector. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of five private-market comparables—BotBuilt, Apis Cor, Unlimited Industries, ADMARES, and Hedral—with no direct public trading comps available in this frontier subsector.

The stage-progression method, the applicable triangulation approach given available data, uses the company's $2M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression. This method yields an implied valuation of $5M. The methodology reflects standard venture capital practice in which seed-stage valuations are anchored to capital deployed and adjusted for expected milestone achievement between financing rounds.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $4M to $6M, with a median point of $5M. The low bound ($4M) and high bound ($6M) reflect reasonable variance around the stage-progression result, accounting for typical uncertainty in early-stage venture valuation. Key limitations include reliance on a single applicable method due to sparse public comps and the inherent uncertainty of seed-stage companies. A more refined range would benefit from additional comparable transaction data or pro-forma revenue multiples once the company reaches later development milestones.
